theories_of_action.summary: Affirmative DVRO petition by Michael against Christina under Family Code § 6320(c) — coercive control via third-party orchestration
statutory_basis: Family Code § 6320(a) — enjoinable behaviors (stalking, harassing, contacting, disturbing the peace)
Family Code § 6320(c) — 'disturbing the peace' includes conduct committed 'directly or indirectly, including through the use of a third party'; coercive control definition
Family Code § 6320(c)(1) — isolating from sources of support
Family Code § 6320(c)(3) — controlling/monitoring movements, communications, finances
theories_of_action.factual_basis: 16-year pattern: Christina acting in concert with Ann Hillberg (staged civil standbys, 911 calls using dispatcher language, coordinated child movement across jurisdictions, triple filings with grandparent visitation petitions) and Ryan McClaran (SIM swaps, proxy communication network, device-proximity requirements). Pattern documented in project_familylaw_orchestration.md, project_communications_fraud.md, project_ryan_mcclaran_it.md.
theories_of_action.strength: STRONG — § 6320(c) as amended by SB 50 (effective 2026-01-01) is textually designed for this pattern. The 'through a third party' language is the explicit statutory capture.
theories_of_action.status: THEORY IDENTIFIED — steward decision required on whether to pursue

theories_of_action.summary: Defense against Christina's Marin DVRO (FL0002067) — challenge factual basis using documented pattern
statutory_basis: Family Code § 6203 — abuse definition (Christina's allegations must meet this threshold)
Family Code § 3011(b) — substantial independent corroboration prerequisite
Family Code § 6323(d) — court shall consider third-person-present or denial of visitation
theories_of_action.factual_basis: Christina's 2025 Marin DVRO petition is the latest iteration of the 16-year counter-filing playbook documented in project_christina_pattern.md. The 2009-06-11 OPD report fabrication finding, the OPD records pickup confirming the 6/2/2009 report is missing, and the § 3011(b) corroboration requirement all undercut the factual foundation.
theories_of_action.strength: MODERATE — depends on court willingness to look behind Christina's declaration to the underlying pattern

theories_of_action.summary: Challenge Sala Ajaniku's September 2010 mediator appointment for failure to meet § 3164(b)/§ 1815/§ 1816 qualifications
statutory_basis: Family Code § 3164(b) — 'shall meet the minimum qualifications required of a counselor of conciliation as provided in Section 1815'
Family Code § 1815(a) — seven mandatory qualification elements
Family Code § 1816 — 16-hour advanced DV training + 4-hour annual + court notification
theories_of_action.factual_basis: No verifiable professional credential found for Sala Ajaniku across 8 public licensing/directory sources. Her September 2010 recommendation reversed Judge Thompson's protective custody order. PRA request drafted (drafts/ajaniku_pra_request_letter.md) to obtain institutional credential records.

theories_of_action.summary: Tom Bane Act (Civil Code § 52.1) claim against Christina and/or Hillberg for interference with constitutional rights by threat/intimidation/coercion
statutory_basis: Civil Code § 52.1(b)-(c) — private right of action for interference with constitutional or statutory rights
Civil Code § 52.1(n) — state immunity does not apply to peace officers
theories_of_action.factual_basis: The orchestration pattern (staged 911 calls, unauthorized civil standbys, fabricated police reports, coordinated child removal across jurisdictions) constitutes interference by threat/intimidation/coercion with Michael's custody rights, parental rights, and liberty interests.
theories_of_action.strength: MODERATE — Bane Act requires 'threat, intimidation, or coercion' which is a higher bar than negligence; the orchestration pattern may meet it but requires careful factual pleading

strategic_notes: T1 (affirmative DVRO) and T2 (Marin defense) are NOT mutually exclusive. Filing an affirmative DVRO in Alameda while defending in Marin is a legitimate two-front strategy.
T3 (Ajaniku qualifications) is a standalone attack on the 2010 custody reversal. If successful, it reopens the custody foundation — which then strengthens both T1 and T2.
T4 (Bane Act) is independent of the Family Code theories and can be filed in any superior court. It provides a damages remedy that the DVRO theories do not.
The federal § 1983 complaint (already drafted, separate workflow) addresses the state-actor dimension. These state theories address the private-party dimension.
STEWARD DECISION REQUIRED: which theory to file first, and in which venue.
